jobs.title: Head of Product - Business Banking
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In 1851, a New York bookkeeper named George D. Lyman observed the same absurd ritual each afternoon: porters carried bags of coins and bundles of checks bank to bank down Wall Street, settling by hand, a fortune exposed to error and theft. Lyman's fix: send everything through one central office and settle the net. On October 11, 1853, in the basement of 14 Wall Street, 52 banks cleared $22.6 million in a single sitting. Money between banks had stopped being an event and became seamless infrastructure.

A century and a half later, the hard part is unchanged: moving money once is easy; making it work every time, for hundreds of thousands of businesses, across every rail, is hard. The bank account is where a company's financial life happens - payroll clears or it doesn't; a wire lands or a deal slips; the month closes clean, or someone loses a weekend to it. Mercury is building a business banking* product at a scale better than anything else in the market.

Business Banking is the heart of Mercury. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving deposit and payment growth, and owning business performance.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Key responsibilities:

- Own the P&L, strategy, and product offering: accounts, user experience, payments, new rails, and agents

- Build AI - and data-driven user experiences at scale better than the alternatives

- Build and scale the org: recruit and lead a high-performing PM team, instill strong build discipline, develop future leaders, and set an operating cadence and culture that drives pace and quality

- Deepen the core account and take new products 0-1 to scale: optimize what businesses run on, and invest in new rails, capabilities, and agents so customers can focus on building their companies

- Make reliability and trust product features: own uptime, correctness, latency, and support outcomes, and be measured on them

- Align the banking ecosystem: bring product, engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, legal, marketing, sales, support, and partners behind one cohesive strategy

Some things that might make you successful in a role like this:

- A leader with great product chops, commercial instinct to grow the business, and discipline to run it safely

- A high bar for craft – leading a creative, customer-centered, data-driven and experimentation-oriented approach

- Enthusiasm for building AI- and agent-powered products that drive spectacular customer experiences

- Exceptional cross-functional leadership across engineering, design, risk, compliance, finance, and partners

- 10+ years' experience, ideally in banking, payments, platforms, or financial products

- 5+ years leading product managers: hiring, coaching, org design, and performance management

- Command of how business banking works: account opening and KYB, deposits and liquidity, payment rails (ACH, wire, check, international, FedNow, RTP)

- Experience launching and scaling 0-1 financial products, ideally in fintech or another high-growth environment, alongside operating a large product with real customers on it

- Sound judgment in a regulated, risk-sensitive environment: balance a delightful experience with the controls a banking product requires, and know which corners are never worth cutting

jobs.title: Head of Product - Business Lending
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In 1910, a Norfolk lawyer named Arthur Morris kept seeing the same thing: a steadily employed worker needed a small loan, the banks turned him away for lack of collateral, and he was left with nowhere reputable to borrow. Morris decided a banking system that shut out most of the people it was meant to serve had a "weak spot" worth fixing, so he built a lender that lent on character and steady income, backed by two references and repaid in small installments. What made it matter wasn't any single loan, but that Morris turned the idea into a repeatable system and scaled it to more than a hundred Morris Plan banks across thirty-seven states.

A century later, the hard part is unchanged: making one good loan is easy; building a business that makes millions of them well is hard. Mercury is building a banking*-grade lending business, where credit extends the trust businesses already place in us to hold and move their money. We need a leader to turn that foundation into a thriving, responsibly-scaled business.

We’re looking for a Head of Product to own Mercury's lending business end-to-end: defining product strategy, leading a team of product managers and lending specialists, driving growth, and ultimately owning business performance and P&L outcomes. You will work closely with credit, sales and finance to grow originations while maintaining healthy approval rates, repayment performance, and loss outcomes.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Key responsibilities

- Own the business lending P&L and strategy: Set the multi-year strategy - which products to build, which segments to serve, how to grow originations against economic and credit targets. Own the numbers.

- Build and scale the lending org:   Recruit, develop, and lead a high-performing PM team,strong product build discipline, develop future leaders, and establish the operating cadence and culture that allow a lending business to move quickly without sacrificing rigor.

- Take products from 0-1 to scale:  Launch and grow Mercury's lending products - term loans, lines of credit, and what comes next, and build the experimentation loop that compounds growth post-launch.

- Partner with credit, underwriting, and risk on credit policy, underwriting models, and eligibility.

- Manage capital and lending partners: Work with finance, capital markets, and banking/lending partners to keep the business well-capitalized and structured to scale, and own those relationships.

- Balance growth with rigor: Build a lending business that customers love while meeting the credit, risk, and compliance standards a regulated product demands— making the hard tradeoffs between speed, experience, and controls.

- Align the lending ecosystem: Bring together product, engineering, underwriting, risk, credit operations, data, compliance, legal, marketing, sales, support, and external partners to execute a cohesive lending strategy and deliver strong business outcomes.

Some things that might make you successful in a role like this:

- We're looking for a leader who has built and scaled a business lending organization, with great product chops, the commercial instinct to grow it and the credit discipline to grow it responsibly, equally credible on portfolio economics with finance, credit policy with underwriting, and product strategy with engineering.

- 10+ years in lending or credit products, including significant time in SMB, commercial, or business lending, with experience building and running teams.

- 5+ years leading and managing teams of product managers, including hiring, coaching, organizational design, and performance management.

- Deep command of the full lending lifecycle: eligibility, application, underwriting and decisioning, funding, servicing, repayment, and collections — and the credit, risk, and compliance considerations at each stage.

- A track record of owning a lending P&L and its levers: pricing, credit policy, capital structure, loss performance, and unit economics.

- Experience launching and scaling 0-1 lending or credit products, ideally in a fintech or high-growth environment.

- Experience working directly with bank partners, lending partners, or capital markets to structure and fund a lending business.

- Sound judgment in a regulated, risk-sensitive environment: you balance a delightful customer experience with the controls a credit product requires.

- A data-driven, experimentation-oriented approach, and exceptional cross-functional leadership across product, underwriting, finance, compliance, and partners.

jobs.title: Head of Product - Personal Banking
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In 1967, John Shepherd-Barron reached his bank minutes after closing and could not get at his own money. In the bath that evening, he thought of a chocolate bar dispenser and swapped the chocolate for cash. On 27 June, outside a Barclays branch on Enfield High Street, an actor named Reg Varney drew £10 from the world's first cash machine. It took a four-digit code (originally six, until his wife told him nobody remembers six). The bank's hours had stopped being the customer's problem.

Nearly sixty years later, the bar has moved, but the test hasn't: a personal financial product is judged on whether it fits the life of the person using it. People do not read documentation, forgive a confusing screen, or care how the ledger works. They want one place that makes sense of everything — spending, saving, planning, investing — and that anticipates rather than reports: where they stand, what deserves attention, what to do next. Mercury is building personal banking* to that standard.

Personal Banking is how Mercury earns a place in someone's financial life. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving growth and engagement, and owning business performance.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Key responsibilities:

- Build a personal banking experience so good that people tell their friends and colleagues about it

- Own the metrics, product strategy and the propositions we take to our customers, covering personal money management, banking, savings, investments, money movement, and in the future, lending

- Set the craft bar: sweat the details — copy, latency, empty states — that decide whether a consumer product feels inevitable rather than adequate

- Drive the use of AI in products where it makes the experience meaningfully better

- Build and scale the org: recruit and lead a high-performing PM team, instill strong build discipline, develop future leaders, and set a cadence and culture that drives pace and quality

- Grow the business: own acquisition, activation, retention, and the loops that compound,  including how personal banking connects to the businesses Mercury already serves

- Make reliability and trust product features: own uptime, correctness, latency, and support outcomes, and be measured on them

- Align the ecosystem: bring product, engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, legal, marketing, support, and partners behind one cohesive strategy

Some things that might make you successful in a role like this:

- A consumer product leader with taste: you have built products millions of people chose to use, and can point to the decisions that made them work

- You have shipped AI-led products to real consumers and have opinions about what AI makes possible and where it fails

- An exceptionally high bar for craft, and a customer-centered, data-driven, and experimentation-oriented approach

- 10+ years building consumer products, including time owning a product's growth and economics, not only its roadmap

- 5+ years leading product managers: hiring, coaching, org design, and performance management

- Experience launching and scaling 0-1 products, alongside operating a large product with real customers on it

- Exceptional cross-functional leadership across engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, and partners

jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
Open call for Founders / Founding Teams (Product Management / Engineering roles)

In 1973 at Xerox PARC, Bob Metcalfe sketched a way for many computers to share a single wire — borrowing the throughput math from his study of Hawaii's ALOHAnet — and he and David Boggs built it and measured it until it held. Behind Ethernet was a two-person team that turned a contested idea into the measured standard now carrying almost all the world's wired traffic.

At Mercury, we’re looking to accelerate several of our AI products that our customers love like Command, CLI, and MCP.  We’re building for ambitious people of all kinds, and are a company made of founders and small technical teams trying to change the world - as part of that, we’re taking open applications for founders or small technical teams (Eng+) that want to work together on building the AI products of the future.  This isn't a fixed role. We expect the nature of work is changing, and small teams of people paired with AI product surface and autonomy to build can create 10x outcomes. Apply as a small team or as an individual

Here are some things you’ll do on the job:

- Find the problem. Work close enough to customers that you spot what matters before anyone assigns it to you — then decide it's worth building.

- Build and automate the workflow end to end using Command, CLI, MCP, and the rest of our AI stack.

- Ship to customers fast — quick understanding, tight iteration, deploy.

- Measure the impact honestly, then do the next one. Kill what didn't move; double down on what did.

- Run as an autonomous team — pick the target, ship the thing, own the outcome.

You should:

- Have shipped something real -  a product, a tool, a company, or an open-source project people actually use.

- Be dangerous across the stack: PMs who can prototype, engineers with product taste.

- Have strong opinions about AI products and the judgment to recognize fast when one of them is wrong.

- Hands experience building AI products with AI, and knowledge about RAG, evals, agent harnesses a plus

- Move fast and measure. Expect most experiments to fail and treat that as the price of finding the ones that don't.

- Care about craft where it's impactful and resist polishing what isn't.

- Communicate clearly and own outcomes - we want real business impact, customer time/pain saved, and a path to scaling what works

Learn more about what we're building:

- Mercury Command — Complete financial work end-to-end with AI. Tell Mercury what to do in natural language; it stages the action and executes with your approval.

- Mercury MCP & CLI — Give your AI agents direct access to verified financial data, or work with your Mercury account straight from the terminal.

- The bank of the future knows your business — Immad on what we're building toward and why now is the moment.

What happens next?

Submit your application and our recruiting team will follow up. We're genuinely open to connecting with founders and teams at any stage — whether you're a strong fit for something we're actively building toward right now, or this is the start of a longer relationship we pick back up when the opportunity is right. If you're building, we want to know you.

jobs.title: Product Marketing Lead - Growth & Revenue
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
By the 1970s, the travel industry had quietly figured out something that most businesses hadn't: growth at scale required three different go-to-market motions happening at once. Individual travelers booked directly — they walked in, called up, and bought. Corporate travel programs needed a sales rep to negotiate rates and sign contracts. And then there were travel agents: independent businesses with deep client relationships who effectively decided what their clients bought. The airlines and hotel chains that grew fastest were the ones that recognized all of these distribution motions and invested in each of them in the right ways.

Mercury runs the same three motions. Most of our growth is self-serve and product-led: Founders discover us, sign up, and stay. Our fast-growing sales team closes meaningful deals with larger businesses. And our partners — incorporators, accountants, investors, and platforms that already have the trust of the businesses we want to reach — refer customers to us the same way a great travel agent would: because they believe in our product and its value to their clients. We are looking for a go-to-market leader who can make all three of these motions work harder together with a data-driven strategy and consistent positioning across the customer journey.

What You'll Do

- Own end-to-end GTM strategy across Mercury's three primary growth motions — product-led, sales-led, and partner-led — including segmentation, messaging, and cross-functional execution.

- Manage and grow a team of product marketers and partner marketers supporting these motions today.

- Build and maintain the customer journey, messaging, and infrastructure that works across all three motions: shared value propositions and personas that flex appropriately for self-serve onboarding flows, sales conversations, and partner co-marketing

- Partner closely with the growth product org on strategy and execution for driving top-of-funnel, conversion, activation, and virality.

- Partner with sales leadership on messaging and enablement, from battlecards and objection-handling frameworks to segment-specific playbooks

- Develop Mercury's partner marketing strategy in collaboration with the partnerships team — including co-marketing programs, partner enablement materials, and joint GTM playbooks

- Lead customer and market research to stay ahead of competitive dynamics, identify growth opportunities across segments, and feed insights into product, pricing, and roadmap decisions

- Define and track the PMM metrics that matter for growth — from activation to adoption to advocacy — and use them to continuously improve GTM strategy

You Should Have

- 10+ years of B2B product marketing experience, with full ownership of GTM strategy — not just launch coordination

- Demonstrated experience driving growth across multiple GTM motions; you've run product-led, sales-led, and partner-led programs, and you understand how they interact

- Strong messaging and positioning craft — you can develop a compelling narrative from scratch, test it with customers, and translate it into assets that actually get used by sales and partners

- Revenue mindset — you track contribution to pipeline, activation, and retention, and you know how to use data to argue for, refine, and defend your strategy

- Experience working with sales leadership on messaging and proof points to improve their team’s ability to source pipeline and close deals.

- Ability to lead cross-functional initiatives without direct authority — aligning sales, product, partnerships, and growth teams around a shared GTM plan

Nice to Have

- Fintech, banking*, or financial services experience — familiarity with the regulatory, trust, and competitive dynamics of this space

- Experience at a company that scaled through multiple GTM channels simultaneously, particularly one with a strong PLG foundation that was extending into enterprise and/or channel

- Data fluency — comfortable pulling your own analysis in Amplitude, Hex, Metabase, or SQL rather than waiting on a data team

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Business Lending
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In the days after the 1906 earthquake and fire destroyed most of San Francisco, the city's banks stayed shut, their vaults too hot to open for weeks. Amadeo Giannini, who ran the small Bank of Italy, did the opposite. He set up a makeshift desk on the wharf, a plank laid across two barrels, and began lending. Most of his customers were shopkeepers, fishermen, and tradespeople who had lost everything, including any papers proving who they were. So Giannini lent on a signature and a handshake, betting on the people in front of him. Those loans helped rebuild the city block by block, and, the story goes, every one of them was paid back.

That's the promise of a business loan: capital, offered fairly and fast, to people with the will and the plan to build something. More than a century later, too many growing businesses still hit a version of the closed vault: slow processes, opaque decisions, and paperwork that arrives too late to matter.

At Mercury, we're building lending products that give growing businesses fast, fair, transparent access to the capital that lets them say yes when it counts. We're looking for a Senior PM to own this product end-to-end. You'll blend sharp product instincts with real empathy for business owners, partnering closely with risk, design, data science, engineering, and operations to ship a product that is both responsible and genuinely delightful to use.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What You'll Do:

- Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Mercury's business lending product suite

- Drive the end-to-end customer journey — eligibility and discovery, application, underwriting and decisioning, funding, servicing, and repayment

- Partner with risk and data science to design underwriting and decisioning experiences that balance speed and approval rates with sound credit and compliance controls

- Work with design and engineering to make the application feel effortless, transparent, and trustworthy for business owners

- Collaborate with banking partners, legal, and compliance to ensure the product is regulatory-compliant and operationally sound

- Define and instrument the metrics that matter: conversion, approval and decline rates, time-to-funding, loss performance, repayment health, and customer satisfaction — and use them to prioritize

- Use customer insight, market research, and data to decide what to build next, and make crisp tradeoffs between scope, risk, and speed

- Partner with marketing, sales, and support to launch the product and bring it to the right customers at the right moment

What You Bring:

- 7+ years of product management or aligned experience, with at least 2+ years in lending, credit, payments, or another regulated financial domain

- Experience of building and scaling lending businesses

- A strong grasp of the lending lifecycle: origination, underwriting, servicing, and repayment , and the risk and compliance considerations that come with it

- Proven ability to ship AI-first and iterate on customer-facing products that solve real problems for users

- Technical fluency: comfort partnering deeply with engineers and data scientists while translating complexity for business, risk, and compliance stakeholders

- Strong customer empathy paired with the rigor to balance growth against credit, compliance, and operational realities

- A track record of using data and experimentation to drive decisions and measurable outcomes

- Comfort operating with ambiguity and setting direction in a fast-moving, greenfield product area

In 1949, as Diners Club tells it, Frank McNamara finished dinner in Manhattan and found his wallet at home in another suit. His wife came down and paid. He returned to the same table the following February and settled the bill with a piece of cardboard, honored at twenty-seven restaurants and carried by two hundred people, most of them his friends. A year later there were 42,000.

McNamara solved two problems at once. Acceptance: enough restaurants to make the card worth carrying, and enough diners to make it worth accepting. And credit: thirty unsecured days of it, on nothing but a signature. The networks settled acceptance decades ago. What is left is the credit, and the question of why someone carries this card rather than another one. That is this role.

Mercury is building its first consumer credit card. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to define what it is, ship it, and grow it from a first cohort into a portfolio. The scope is the credit account itself: the acquisition and application funnel, the approval experience and the underwriting decisions behind it, how the line moves over time, what the rewards are worth, and the experience of carrying the account day to day.

About the role

At Mercury, we believe financial operations should be seamless, scalable, and built on a foundation of trust. The Reconciliation team develops the products, processes, and controls that protect the accuracy and integrity of Mercury’s core financial systems and money movement.

jobs.description:
Mercury is building Mercury Bank, N.A., a proposed nationally chartered bank focused on serving ambitious businesses. Credit and lending are central to that mission, and as we migrate our charge card and term loan products to the Bank's own balance sheet and build the next generation of lending infrastructure, we need someone who can hold the full program together.

The Senior Technical Program Manager for Credit and Lending will own end-to-end delivery of the technology programs that power Mercury's charge card, term loan, and adjacent credit products. You will be the connective tissue between Engineering, Product, Risk, Compliance, Treasury, and Operations: setting strategy for how these programs run, surfacing tradeoffs that unblock leaders, sequencing the critical path, and ensuring that what ships is audit-ready from day one.

We are looking for someone who has operated at this level before, in a regulated environment, at scale, with real accountability for outcomes.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What you'll do:

Program ownership

- Own the integrated program plan across all active credit and lending workstreams, covering milestones, dependencies, and critical paths across Engineering, Product, Risk, Compliance, Treasury, and Operations.

- Proactively manage sequencing, resourcing tradeoffs, and escalations. When initiatives are off-track, you identify it first and bring a recommended path forward.

- Ensure Compliance, Treasury, and Operations readiness lands alongside product and regulatory milestones

- Drive incident learnings back into design, test coverage, and runbooks so each issue improves the underlying system, not just fixes the symptom.

- Contribute to the overall (proposed) Mercury Bank, NA technical program, collaborating with other TPMs to build a holistic view of progress and risks

Governance and decision-making

- Keep a single source of truth for status, decisions, risks, and owners. Maintain a living RAID log with clear owners and impact assessments.

- Facilitate structured decision-making by surfacing options and tradeoffs to leaders before problems escalate.

- Build and improve the operating systems that drive credit and lending product decisions: planning cycles, reviews, decision frameworks, launch readiness.

Communication and influence

- Produce concise, predictable updates calibrated to the audience.

- Synthesize complex cross-functional information into recommendations that help executives decide and move.

- Produce documentation of program objectives, architecture decisions, and operational impacts that onboards new team members without requiring a meeting to explain it.

- Function as a trusted thought partner to engineering leads, product managers, and senior leadership.

Execution and improvement

- Identify inefficiencies and eliminate them through automation, AI tooling, or process redesign.

- Lead technical retrospectives and post-mortems, ensuring learnings are systematized rather than forgotten.

What we're looking for:

Experience

- 10+ years of program management or technical program management in a high-growth or regulated environment.

- Direct experience in financial services, fintech, or credit infrastructure. Compliance, audit, reporting and risk management obligations are familiar territory.

- Track record of operating at the department or business level, owning programs with multiple concurrent workstreams and cross-functional accountability.

- Proven ability to communicate with and influence executive stakeholders, in writing and in high-stakes meetings, without a senior manager to translate.

- Bonus: Familiarity with the lending tooling ecosystem such as loan origination, credit risk management and lending management systems.

How you work

- Product-first. You evaluate everything through: what is the user problem, what is the fastest path to learning, what actually moves the needle.

- AI-native. You use AI tools to do your actual work. You have built workflows or tooling that changed how your team operates. When you see a repetitive process, you automate it.

- Comfortable in ambiguity. You build structure where there is none.

- Systems thinker. You see dependencies, second-order effects, and points of failure before they surface, and you build programs that account for them.

- Energized by building and operating. You do your best work designing the system and running it well once it is built.

What you bring:

- Technical fluency. You can understand and challenge engineering decisions, identify technical risks early, and translate complexity for non-technical stakeholders.

- Exceptional written and verbal communication. You write documentation that clarifies hard decisions and build frameworks teams actually adopt.

- Commercial instincts. You understand the financial dynamics of a lending business well enough to evaluate tradeoffs with authority.

- High emotional intelligence. You build trust quickly across engineering, product, risk, and executive stakeholders. You navigate complex interpersonal situations without losing credibility or momentum.
